column12: JUDGEMENT on the comparator and on the indication that sets the price. The engine carries one price per asset. gMG is the lead indication: it reads out first (1H 2027 against 2028-12 for SjD), and Vor calls it 'The Beachhead Indication' (8-K 0001193125-26-009961, exhibit 99.1). Telitacicept is a weekly self-injected pre-filled syringe, so it would be dispensed through pharmacies under Part D. Vyvgart Hytrulo is the gMG incumbent in that setting (86 Part D beneficiaries in 2023 and 658 in 2024). The case against, and it is material: (1) The price also applies to Sjogren's, where no drug is approved and the book prices ianalumab at Benlysta's Part D $37,182, 81% lower. In this seed's own engine run, Sjogren's supplies about half of the plateau revenue at the gMG price. Payers may not accept that price for Sjogren's, and a price set for Sjogren's would cut revenue by about four fifths. (2) Per-beneficiary spend in a product's second year includes partial years, so this understates an annual price. Vyvgart IV reads $254,275 in Part D and $231,053 in Part B (the nipocalimab seed's anchor); Vyvgart Hytrulo reads $167,216 in Part B. (3) A late entrant in a crowded class may price below the incumbent to win formulary position. Zilbrysq and Rystiggo, the other self-administered gMG products, have no rows in the book's CMS table. No US price for telitacicept has been published

column11: Bell CF et al., Lupus Science & Medicine 2020;7(1):e000357, doi:10.1136/lupus-2019-000357 (MarketScan, 1,879 US patients starting belimumab 2011-2015): 26.2% discontinued within six months; at a constant rate 1 - (1 - 0.262)^2 = 0.4554 a year. The book's ianalumab and dazodalibep seeds carry this figure for Sjogren's
column12: JUDGEMENT: one value serves both indications. Belimumab is the closest mechanism (it blocks BLyS, one of telitacicept's two targets), and this figure is what the book's two other Sjogren's seeds use. In gMG the book holds two other figures: 0.5 for the anti-FcRns (nipocalimab seed, real-world efgartigimod persistence) and 0.2704 for a continuous C5 inhibitor (cemdisiran seed, zilucoplan French early access, PMID 41904994). 0.4554 sits between them. The case for lower: telitacicept is continuous weekly therapy, not the cycled dosing that drives anti-FcRn stops, so gMG persistence may be nearer the C5 figure. The case for higher: Bell measured IV belimumab in lupus, and injection-site reactions were 17% on telitacicept against 2% on placebo in the pooled safety set (8-K 0001193125-26-009961, exhibit 99.1)

column11: Vor FY2025 10-K (0001193125-26-130451, filed 2026-03-30), Note 10 'Significant Agreements', Telitacicept License Agreement of 25 June 2025 (book filing_sections): exclusive licence to develop and commercialise telitacicept outside Greater China (mainland China, Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan). Vor 'is responsible for all development, regulatory and commercialization activities and costs in the licensed territory'. Consideration: $45.0mm cash upfront plus a warrant over 16,000,000 shares valued at $177.4mm. RemeGen 'is eligible to receive up to $330.0 million in regulatory milestone payments and up to $3.775 billion in sales milestone payments' and 'tiered royalties on net sales of the Licensed Products in the licensed territory, ranging from high single digit to mid-teen percentages of net sales, subject to customary reductions'. Netted as the book nets a royalty the company pays: (margin - royalty) / margin. Margin from argenx's FY2025 cost rows in the book (lookup.py seed empasiprubart: cogs 0.1086, sga 0.3293, rd 0.3286, other_costs 0.0), 1 - 0.7665 = 0.2335. (0.2335 - 0.07) / 0.2335 = 0.7002
column12: JUDGEMENT twice, and PROVISIONAL. (1) Tier: 'high single digit' is taken at its bottom, 7%. The book's disitamab vedotin seed does the same with RemeGen's identical wording to Seagen, and the litifilimab, VLA15 and ralinepag seeds take their lowest tier too. (2) Margin: Vor is pre-revenue and has no company-level rows in the book, so no margin of its own exists. argenx is the proxy: a single-franchise autoimmune biotech selling the gMG incumbent, with filed FY2025 cost lines. Vor's cost block now borrows argenx's rows, so the margin stands and so does the share; recompute when Vor files a cost of sales. Case against: the tiers rise with sales, and this seed's engine run peaks near $1.4bn of product revenue, so the blended rate is likely above the floor. At 10% the share is 0.5717, at 12% 0.4861 and at the 15% top 0.3576. The up to $3.775bn of sales milestones and $330mm of regulatory milestones are not netted here, as in the book's other royalty seeds. They are large against this build's revenue, and the note records them. RemeGen also takes a single-digit share of sublicence proceeds if Vor sublicenses before a specified development event (same note)

(1) Generalised, not ocular-only: 'A recent population-based study conducted by the Mayo Clinic found that 51% of patients presented with ocular onset, and 55% of these developed generalized symptoms' (section 3.1.2), so 1 - 0.51 x 0.45 = 0.7705. (2) AChR-positive within gMG: 'Eighty-five percent of people with gMG are AChR antibody-positive' (AstraZeneca 6-K 0001654954-26-008478, as the book's cemdisiran seed carries it). (3) MuSK-positive within the AChR-negative 15%: 'Antibodies against MuSK are found in approximately 7-10% of all MG patients and up to 40% of patients with generalized MG who are seronegative for AChR Abs' (section 3.2.1), so 0.15 x 0.40 = 0.06. 0.7705 x (0.85 + 0.06) = 0.701155, or 57,996 US adults

column12: JUDGEMENT: 0.25 of Vyvgart's plateau treated share, the multiple the book's cemdisiran seed takes for its late gMG entrant. The discontinuation ratio turns a share of patients on therapy into a share of starts. The plateau is 0.049094 / 0.4554 = 10.78% of the eligible pool, about 6,250 US patients. Case for higher: on Vor's cross-trial chart, telitacicept's China Phase 3 (240 mg, RemeGen-sponsored) shows the largest placebo-adjusted MG-ADL change at week 24 across efgartigimod, nipocalimab, rozanolixizumab, ravulizumab, eculizumab, zilucoplan and inebilizumab. Its BAFF/APRIL mechanism is one that none of the gMG products on Vor's competitor list uses (FcRn, C5, CD19; 10-K 0001193125-26-130451). The deck also claims continuous self-injection and 'No Burdensome Vaccination Requirements' (8-K 0001193125-26-009961, exhibit 99.1; the comparisons are cross-trial, not head-to-head). Case for lower: it would reach the US around 2029, behind three anti-FcRns (Vyvgart, Rystiggo, Imaavy), the C5s (Soliris and its biosimilars, Ultomiris, Zilbrysq, with cemdisiran and gefurulimab under review) and Uplizna (Vor 10-K competitor list; cemdisiran seed). It needs weekly injections, the global Phase 3 has not read out, China effect sizes may not carry to a global population, and Vor has never launched a product. 'More than 10,000 patients' may count patients ever treated, which would overstate Vyvgart's peak

column12: JUDGEMENT: telitacicept is modelled as a follower behind ianalumab (filed Q1 2026 under priority review, ianalumab seed), with the same measured follower ratio as dazodalibep. Its discontinuation equals theirs (0.4554), so no conversion is needed. Case for lower: it would be the third entrant, behind ianalumab and dazodalibep (OASIZ 301 positive 2026-09-22), with nipocalimab and efgartigimod Sjogren's programmes also running (dazodalibep seed). It would also sell at the gMG-anchored price, five times the Benlysta price that measured this uptake. Case for higher: in RemeGen's China Phase 3, ESSDAI fell 4.4 points on 160 mg and 3.0 on 80 mg against 0.6 on placebo at week 24, p<0.0001 (8-K 0001193125-26-009961, exhibit 99.1). The same deck calls this the largest placebo-adjusted ESSDAI reduction across Phase 2 and 3 datasets, at 4.3 points, cross-trial and not head-to-head. Vor calls it the only therapy with significant gains in both ESSDAI and ESSPRI (8-K 0001193125-26-261661, exhibit 99.2, the NMPA approval release).
